test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Who described the kingdom of Awadh as 'a cherry that will drop into our mouth one day'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie.**__

__
 
• **Lord Dalhousie **described the kingdom of Awadh as "a cherry that will drop into our mouth one day". 
 
• He said this in 1851. In 1856, the kingdom was formally annexed to the British Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856):

 
 
• Opened the first Railway line from Bombay to Thane in 1853.
 
• Doctrine of Lapse.
 
• Established Postal system.
 
• Passed Widow Remarriage Bill.
 
 
 
• Lord Cornwallis (1786-1793):
 
 
• Introduced - Permanent Settlement of Bengal and Zamindari System.
 
• Police reforms.
 
• Introduced Civil Services in India.
 
 
 
• Lord Curzon (1899-1905):
 
 
• Partition of Bengal in 1905 into 2 provinces: Bengal and East Bengal.
 
• Passed Ancient Monuments Act in 1904.
 
• Established Archaeological Survey of India.
 
 
 
• Lord Henry Hardinge (1910-1916):
 
 
• Attempted to modernize the equipment of the army.
 
• Capital shifted to Delhi from Kolkata.
